# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

I see display `0`, an orange light, and three wires in order: red, yellow, blue. I am sending this complete visual information to the Blind so they can match it against what they can feel, and to the Mute so they can interpret the manual and advise the Blind. The gestures from the Mute are not yet meaningful to me without an established code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, light orange, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, light orange, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell the Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The display remains `0` and the wires remain red, yellow, blue, but the light has changed from orange to green. I should report the current state to both teammates; the Mute can use the manual to determine whether this change indicates the next step, and the Blind can act if instructed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light is now green, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light is now green, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Check the manual and instruct the Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The light has changed again, now to red, while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. I also saw the Mute’s 👎 gesture, but its meaning has not been established, so I should not infer an action from it. I will report the state to both teammates and ask the Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light is now red, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light is now red, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I saw your 👎 gesture but do not know its meaning. Please use the manual and instruct the Blind.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has cycled back to orange; display `0` and wire colours are unchanged. No new gesture arrived. I will relay the current state and ask the Mute to send the manual’s required operation to the Blind through me if necessary.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light orange, wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No new instruction arrived.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, light orange, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please give the Blind the exact required action via a gesture code I can relay in words.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is green again; the display and wire colours are unchanged. I see the Mute’s two `☝` gestures and the Blind’s `👍`, but no meaning has been agreed for these signs, so they are not safe instructions. I will establish a clear relay protocol: the Mute can signal the required operation with named gestures, and I will speak that interpretation to the Blind. The Blind should not act on the existing gestures.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. I saw Mute gesture ☝ ☝ and you gesture 👍, but those signs have no agreed meaning. Do not act on them yet. I am establishing a gesture relay protocol.")
speak(to="mute", text="I saw your gestures ☝ ☝, but their meaning is not established. Please use a clear sequence and I will relay it: first gesture names the operation, second names the target. Operation codes: 👍 press, 👎 cut, 👌 toggle, ✊ hold, 🖐 wait. Target codes: ☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖐 display, 🤞 light. Signal the exact manual instruction.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 🖐 👍 👍 🖐 👍 👍 👍]

The Mute’s `👎 ✌` matches the relay protocol I proposed: `👎` means cut and `✌` means wire 2. The Blind’s gestures have no established meaning for me, so I will not infer anything from them. I will tell the Blind to cut the yellow second wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute's instruction is: cut wire 2, the yellow wire. Current display 0 and light red; wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```
